note: Trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column on every insert/update. Touches no table.

In ONE transaction: add nullable column customer_id_new bigint (metadata only, no rewrite), NOT VALID checks (not null, equal to customer_id) that already apply to new rows, and the sync trigger. lock_timeout 200ms + retry, so app queries never queue behind us for more than 200ms. If the lock is never obtained the step fails with nothing changed.
Backfill ids [1, 1000001) in 5000-row batches, one commit per batch, short pause between batches. Row locks only on old rows the app never updates.
Vacuum so the next batches reuse the space of the dead row versions (limits table bloat). No truncation, so no exclusive lock.
Backfill ids from 9000001 up to the current max(id). Orders inserted since the trigger was created already have the value and are skipped.
Vacuum and analyze, so the new column has planner statistics before it becomes customer_id.
Validate 'customer_id_new IS NOT NULL'. Scans the table under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or inserts. Fails (plan stops, app unaffected) if any row was missed.
Validate 'customer_id_new = customer_id' on every row: proves every value was copied unchanged. Same non-blocking lock.

Swap, in ONE short transaction under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (lock_timeout 200ms + retry): drop the trigger and the equality check, SET NOT NULL (no table scan, because the validated check already proves there are no NULLs), drop the now-redundant check, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. All metadata only, so the lock is held for milliseconds. Queued app queries then see customer_id as bigint NOT NULL; the app's SQL is unchanged, so no deploy is needed.
Remove the trigger function (no longer used).
Check the result: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL and has no NULLs.
